title: needs-decision: idd-doctor's cleanup-backlog "mirrors CI" claim doesn't match the actual CI workflow
body:
## Background

`docs/idd-helper-scripts.md` (~L360, mirrored verbatim in
`idd-template/docs/idd-helper-scripts.md`) and `src/scripts/idd-doctor.mts`'s
`--help` text (~L4272, generated into `scripts/idd-doctor.mjs`) both state
that a local run during a merge burst should pass
`--cleanup-backlog-window-days 1` to keep it fast, "mirroring CI." The
originating issue, #1145 (closed), records the same claim as background
fact: "CI already sidesteps this with `--cleanup-backlog-window-days 1`."

Directly verified against the current `.github/workflows/idd-doctor.yml`:
its only invocation is `run: node scripts/idd-doctor.mjs`, with no
arguments at all — every CI run uses the default 14-day window, not
`--cleanup-backlog-window-days 1`. The claim that CI "already sidesteps"
this, or "mirrors" a short window, does not match the current workflow
file. (`idd-template/` does not ship an `idd-doctor.yml` at all — this
half of the mismatch is source-repo-only; the misleading `--help` text
in `idd-doctor.mts` is distributed to adopters who copy the script,
independent of whether their own repo runs it in CI.)

Observed cost: a local `node scripts/idd-doctor.mjs` run (part of this
repository's own `pre-push-validate` chain) scanned merged PRs in the
14-day default window, issuing one serial `gh api .../issues/<n>/comments`
call per merged PR (193 PRs at the time of observation) -- exceeding a
120s timeout and completing only after roughly 280s. If CI runs the
identical unflagged invocation on every `pull_request` trigger, it likely
pays a comparable cost on every single PR.

## Proposed change

No single proposed change: this is a maintainer decision between which
side of the mismatch to fix, mirroring the decision pattern #2567,
#2091, #2181, and #2377 already used for a related class of problem
(a documented assumption drifting from shipped configuration).

### Options for a maintainer to choose among

1. **Wire `--cleanup-backlog-window-days` into CI** -- add the flag
   (e.g. `1`, or another short value) to
   `.github/workflows/idd-doctor.yml`'s `run: node scripts/idd-doctor.mjs`
   step, matching the originally documented intent. A short per-PR window
   is plausible here specifically because the check re-runs on every PR:
   a rolling short window can still provide cumulative multi-day backlog
   coverage across successive runs, at a fraction of the per-run cost.
2. **Correct the documentation instead** -- if CI intentionally uses the
   full 14-day window (for example because per-PR coverage should not
   assume every intervening PR also ran the check), update
   `docs/idd-helper-scripts.md` and `idd-doctor.mts`'s `--help` text (and
   the `idd-template/docs/idd-helper-scripts.md` mirror) to stop claiming
   this "mirrors CI," stating instead that only a manual/local run
   benefits from the flag.
3. **Something else the maintainer prefers** (for example lowering the
   default window, or having the workflow pass a different value
   depending on trigger type).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A maintainer states which option above to take (or a different
      resolution) in a comment on this issue.
- [ ] Close this issue once that decision is recorded. The chosen option
      becomes a follow-up `ready` issue scoped to the exact
      config/workflow/doc change.

## Candidate files

- `.github/workflows/idd-doctor.yml`
- `docs/idd-helper-scripts.md`
- `idd-template/docs/idd-helper-scripts.md`
- `src/scripts/idd-doctor.mts` (and generated `scripts/idd-doctor.mjs`)

---

_Autopilot suitability: 3 / 5 -- higher is more autopilot-suitable;
below the configured floor is human-oriented. This is a policy/capacity
trade-off between CI thoroughness and per-run cost; the factual evidence
above is settled and does not need re-deriving._
